decisions.rationale: Lead Floette-Eternal and Farigiraf to threaten Trick Room into the rain mode while Floette pressures Swampert and Basculegion. Mawile is the primary Trick Room mega cleaner; Heliolisk gives a fast rain-immune option and Electric pressure if Raichu is omitted.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 durable: opponent led Pelipper + Mega Swampert, used Tailwind immediately, and brought Basculegion and Archaludon; Raichu and Tsareena were omitted. Pelipper is Damp Rock with Hurricane, Hydro Pump, Tailwind, Protect; Basculegion is Choice Scarf Adaptability; Archaludon is Shuca Berry with Electro Shot, Draco Meteor, Flash Cannon, Protect. Floette-Mega + Farigiraf is a strong rain plan: Trick Room offsets Tailwind, Energy Ball pressures Swampert/Basculegion, and Helping Hand Moonblast pressures Archaludon/Pelipper. Respect a potential Raichu/Lightning Rod adjustment before committing Heliolisk.

decisions.rationale: Lead Pelipper and Swampert to immediately set Drizzle and pressure with Swift Swim Mega Swampert. Basculegion and Archaludon provide powerful backline sweepers.

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand acts before Floette’s attack and makes Energy Ball a guaranteed OHKO on Mega Swampert across its legal bulk range. Mega Evolving improves Floette’s offensive profile without compromising its Trick Room move order here.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 confirmed opponent’s backline was Choice Scarf Adaptability Basculegion and Shuca Berry Stamina Archaludon; Raichu and Tsareena were omitted. Pelipper is Damp Rock with Hurricane, Hydro Pump, Tailwind, Protect. Floette can Mega Evolve with Floettite; Mega Floette has Fairy Aura and improved special offense. Helping Hand-boosted Energy Ball is a guaranteed OHKO on Mega Swampert across legal bulk ranges, while unboosted Energy Ball is only a possible OHKO. Against Pelipper/Mega Swampert rain structures, prioritize Trick Room and immediate Swampert removal; keep Lightning Rod in mind if Raichu is present before using Heliolisk’s Electric attacks.

decisions.rationale: Under Trick Room, Floette-Eternal acts before us. Pelipper hits Farigiraf with a rain-boosted Hydro Pump for high damage, and Swampert-Mega finishes Farigiraf with Waterfall to remove its Armor Tail support and Trick Room setter.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Floette-Eternal and Farigiraf confirmed. Farigiraf has Armor Tail and used Trick Room. Swampert-Mega and Pelipper outspeed under Tailwind but move after foes in Trick Room.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper stays in to attack under Rain while Archaludon enters to threaten strong Electric/Dragon pressure against Floette-Mega and Farigiraf.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Floette-Eternal and Farigiraf confirmed. Farigiraf has Armor Tail and used Trick Room. Bring Archaludon into the fainted Swampert slot.

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand resolves before Floette, and boosted Fairy Aura Moonblast is a guaranteed KO on Pelipper. Floette then acts before either foe under Trick Room and survives an unboosted Archaludon Flash Cannon from full; if Pelipper Protects, it cannot combine Hurricane with Flash Cannon this turn.

Pelipper: Damp Rock, Drizzle, Hurricane, Hydro Pump, Tailwind, Protect. Mega Floette has Fairy Aura. Helping Hand + Mega Floette Energy Ball guarantees Mega Swampert OHKO; unboosted is only possible. Helping Hand + Fairy Aura Moonblast guarantees Pelipper OHKO across legal bulk; unboosted Moonblast is only a possible OHKO. decisions.rationale: Bring Mawile: it is exceptionally slow for the remaining Trick Room turns and gives the strongest immediate endgame pressure alongside Mega Floette. Heliolisk is faster and more fragile here; Mawile also retains useful Steel/Fairy defensive utility against the likely remaining rain backline.

Floette is immune to Dragon, and Mawile is immune to Dragon. Flash Cannon hits Floette-Mega super-effectively. Last Respects hits Mawile heavily. Tailwind expires this turn, and Trick Room is active, so we want powerful attacks before speed changes.

Energy Ball and Thunderbolt each guarantee the KO on Basculegion from its displayed HP. Doubling removes any dependence on the final Trick Room speed ordering; Basculegion is Choice-locked into an attack Heliolisk is immune to.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Game 1 and Game 2 brought Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Choice Scarf Adaptability Basculegion, and Shuca Berry Stamina Archaludon; Raichu and Tsareena were omitted in both observed games. Pelipper: Damp Rock Drizzle, Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect. Mega Swampert: Waterfall/Earthquake/Ice Punch/Protect. Basculegion: Adamant Choice Scarf Adaptability, Wave Crash/Last Respects/Flip Turn/Aqua Jet; Mega Mawile Sucker Punch OHKOs it if attacking. reflections.summary: Won game 2 and the series 2-0 because the Floette/Farigiraf Trick Room mode directly punished Pelipper’s Tailwind lead: Floette protected while Farigiraf established Trick Room, then Helping Hand-boosted Mega Floette removed Mega Swampert and Pelipper immediately. This left the opponent without rain pressure or speed control and allowed Floette to finish Archaludon while Mawile’s Intimidate and Sucker Punch contained Basculegion. The between-game approach helped rather than backfired: the same revealed rain core was answered by a well-suited four of Mega Floette, Farigiraf, Mega Mawile, and Heliolisk. Mega Floette was the correct evolution; its Fairy Aura-boosted damage and Energy Ball coverage were decisive. Preparation was strong: the registered six included a dedicated rain answer in Heliolisk and an effective Trick Room/Fairy mode, while Camerupt, Palafin, Liepard, and Mega Chandelure were not shown to offer a clearer answer than the brought four. The main caveat is that Heliolisk was largely insurance rather than central to the win, so its value depended on Basculegion surviving longer or rain remaining relevant.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, retain Mega Floette + Farigiraf as the primary answer to this Pelipper/Mega Swampert rain structure and prioritize Trick Room over trying to race Tailwind. Continue Mega Evolving Floette rather than Mawile when the opponent presents Swampert/Pelipper/Archaludon, since Floette’s boosted Energy Ball and Moonblast create the key knockouts. Bring Mawile to Intimidate and threaten Scarf Basculegion with Sucker Punch, but avoid relying on Sucker Punch alone if Basculegion can exploit Last Respects after teammates faint. Heliolisk remains a sound fourth for rain immunity and late-game cleanup, though Palafin or Mega Camerupt would only merit consideration if future evidence shows a different opposing four or stronger anti-Trick Room coverage.
reflections.notebook: Opponent repeatedly selected Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Choice Scarf Adaptability Basculegion, and Shuca Berry Stamina Archaludon; Raichu and Tsareena were omitted in both games. Their apparent default plan is Drizzle plus Pelipper Tailwind supporting Mega Swampert, with Archaludon and Scarf Basculegion as offensive follow-up. Pelipper carries Damp Rock, Hurricane, Hydro Pump, Tailwind, Protect. Swampert carries Waterfall, Earthquake, Ice Punch, Protect. Basculegion carries Wave Crash, Last Respects, Flip Turn, Aqua Jet and can be locked into Last Respects; Mawile Sucker Punch OHKOs it if it attacks. Archaludon carries Electro Shot, Draco Meteor, Flash Cannon, Protect; Shuca Berry softens Ground coverage, and Flash Cannon threatens Farigiraf but does not OHKO full Mega Floette alone. Floette/Farigiraf Trick Room is an effective structural counter to Pelipper Tailwind. Helping Hand + Mega Floette Energy Ball removes Mega Swampert, and Helping Hand + Fairy Aura Moonblast removes Pelipper. Mega Floette is the preferred Mega against this core; Mawile is valuable as Intimidate and Basculegion pressure. Heliolisk is useful rain-insurance and a safe late-game option.

reflections.summary: The series and game were lost because opponent's Trick Room setup (Farigiraf) combined with heavy offensive threats (Mega Floette-Eternal and Mawile) exploited our rain speed-control strategy. Bringing Pelipper and Mega Swampert into a team featuring Farigiraf and Trick Room backfired completely, as we walked straight into a reverse speed room on Turn 1 and got dismantled by slow, hard-hitting answers.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent's Trick Room core (Farigiraf, Mega Floette, Mawile, Heliolisk), abandon the rain-speed dependency. Instead, bring anti-Trick Room or faster stall-breaking options from the draft, such as Feraligatr or Altaria, and focus heavily on preventing Trick Room rather than trying to outspeed under it.
reflections.notebook: Opponent runs a potent Trick Room team featuring Armor Tail Farigiraf, Mega Floette-Eternal (Fairy Aura), Mega Mawile (Intimidate), and Focus Sash Dry Skin Heliolisk. They heavily rely on Farigiraf setting Trick Room with redirection or support (Helping Hand), letting slow powerhouses like Floette and Mawile sweep under the altered dimensions. In future series, prioritize denying Trick Room over setting rain.
